notes: Garfield is designated as a Qualified Urban Aid (QUA) municipality and therefore has only a rehabilitation (present need) obligation of 322 units and zero prospective (new construction) obligation for the Fourth Round. The City adopted a binding resolution on January 21, 2025. Court case docket is BER-L-000506-25. A May 5, 2025 court order initially listed rehabilitation as zero, but the Town Attorney confirmed this was an error; the DCA-determined rehabilitation obligation is 322 units. The HEFSP was filed May 22, 2025. Because the obligation is rehabilitation-only and Garfield is a dense urban city, specific development sites in the conventional sense (block/lot rezoning for new construction) were not surfaced in search results. No individual inclusionary or redevelopment sites found in available snippets.

notes: Court set Fourth Round obligations on May 19, 2025: Present Need = 0, Prospective Need = 188. The Borough also had a prior obligation from the New Jersey Builders Association (NJBA) settlement for prospective need of 188 units. Per the December 15, 2025 settlement agreement with FSHC, the Borough's Fourth Round RDP (Realistic Development Potential) is 12 affordable units. The HEFSP was adopted June 24, 2025 and filed June 25, 2025. A Borough Council Special Meeting was held June 26, 2025. An amendment to the HEFSP was prepared in February 2026 to be consistent with the December 2025 FSHC settlement. Implementing ordinances Ord. 794-26 (amended affordable housing chapter) and Ord. 795-26 (affordable housing overlay expansion) were adopted March 16, 2026. The overlay expansion under Ord. 795-26 designates specific blocks/lots presently zoned B-2 and R-1 for inclusionary development (15% rental / 20% for-sale). Bergen County Utilities Authority (BCUW) has 60 days from January 5, 2026 to perform due diligence on Borough-owned parcels for a group home; if viable it counts toward the 12-unit RDP.

The Borough's prior Housing Element and Fair Share Plan from 2019 was referenced in zoning code. Existing senior housing (Hasbrouck Heights Senior Housing, Housing Authority of Bergen County) provides existing affordable units.
